analysis: This batch adds optional per-chip earnings types to desktop-app/src/shared/contracts.ts (ChipModelEarning, lines 193-199; NetworkData.by_chip and by_chip_window, lines 204-206), plus tests, a fixture and developer docs. The changes are type-only and test/docs-only. I examined them against the provider threat model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-011, A-001, A-008, A-015/A-016, T-041). None touches the coordinator-provider WebSocket contract, attestation, App Attest authorization, key handling, prefix-cache storage, fan helper or inference paths. The new data is untrusted coordinator-supplied earnings statistics used only for UI ranking of recommended models. The tests show malformed data is rejected: machines of 0, negative or fractional micro-USD strings, non-string chip, a missing window and stale as_of (over 5 minutes) all fall back to network totals. Data flow is one-way into display and ranking, and the docs say the recommendation autopilot action still only sends models, pinned and downloads, which the Swift side validates. Residual question: the implementation in desktop-app/src/renderer/features/models/recommendations.ts is not supplied in this batch. Whether it parses the bigint strings safely, caps the number of rows and bounds the output of a malicious or compromised coordinator cannot be checked. This is an integration concern, not a defect in these files. A manipulated ranking could steer a user toward downloading a catalog model, but Swift enforces the catalog and eligibility checks, so no concrete security regression is identified. The test fixture contains no secrets.
